Commercial Printing Services for Direct Mail Campaigns

In-house printing built for mail. Postcards, self-mailers, letters, brochures, and newsletters produced at our New Paltz facility and moved directly into mail prep.

Cornerstone prints commercial direct mail pieces for Hudson Valley businesses — postcards, brochures, letters, envelopes, catalogs, and custom formats — all to USPS automation specs. Commercial printing for direct mail differs from general commercial print because every piece has to meet postal specifications for size, paper weight, aspect ratio, and machinability. We design and print to spec the first time, so nothing comes back surcharged or rejected at the BMEU.

Commercial printing built for mail

A lot of printers can put ink on paper. Fewer are set up to handle the full workflow from file review to printed piece to postal-ready mail.

Our commercial printing work is built around direct mail requirements. That means we look at more than color and finish. We also review size, thickness, folds, aspect ratio, addressing areas, tabbing requirements, and other details that affect postage and mailability.

If a piece is meant to mail, it should be designed and printed with mailing in mind from the start. We've seen too many campaigns get derailed because a printer approved a file without checking whether it meets USPS automation standards or qualifies for presort discounts.

What we print

We print a wide range of direct-mail and business communication formats, including:

Postcards
Standard and jumbo sizes — 4×6, 6×9, 6×11 — on heavy cardstock

Whether you need a short-run digital job or a larger campaign, we match the format and production method to the job.

Postcard printing services

Postcards remain one of the most effective direct mail formats because they are easy to read, cost-efficient to mail, and fast to produce. We print postcards in common direct mail sizes such as 4×6, 6×9, and 6×11, with stock and coating options based on your campaign goals.

For many local and regional campaigns, postcards are the simplest way to combine visibility, speed, and response. A Hudson Valley nonprofit running a donor reactivation campaign saw a 23% response rate using 6×9 postcards with variable data personalization — well above their historical email performance.

Direct mail printing and mailing

Because Cornerstone Services also handles mailing, your project does not need to leave one vendor for another after it comes off press. That reduces delays, prevents handoff mistakes, and keeps the campaign moving.

We can print, address, sort, prep, and induct mail with one coordinated workflow. For clients running recurring campaigns — monthly newsletters, quarterly appeals, seasonal promotions — that saves time and keeps production more predictable.

One Ulster County property management company coordinates 12 mailings per year through our facility. Their turnaround from final file to mail drop averages 4 business days because we eliminate the print-to-mail handoff.

Learn more about direct mail campaigns →

Variable data printing

Variable data printing allows you to personalize each printed piece with different names, addresses, offers, neighborhoods, account details, or other fields.

This is especially useful for:

  • Customer reactivation campaigns
  • Nonprofit donor appeals
  • Municipal notices and tax communications
  • Real estate farming
  • Segmented offers by audience or geography

If your campaign performs better with personalization, variable data printing gives you a way to scale it without creating separate jobs manually. We've run campaigns with thousands of unique versions — same layout, different content matched to each recipient.

Digital and offset printing options

Not every print job should be produced the same way. Some campaigns need short-run flexibility and fast turnarounds. Others need larger quantities and lower unit costs.

We use digital and offset production based on quantity, timeline, versioning, and finish requirements. The goal is not to force every job into one press method — it is to choose the method that fits the project.

Digital Printing

Best for runs under 5,000 pieces, jobs with variable data, or campaigns that need quick turnaround.

Offset Printing

Best for runs above 5,000 where unit cost matters and the content is static. Lower cost per piece at volume.

Our process

1

File review and preflight

We review artwork for bleed, resolution, color mode, layout, and mailing compatibility before anything goes to press.

2

Proof approval

You receive a proof before production begins. We do not print until you approve.

3

Printing

Your job is produced on the equipment that best fits the quantity and format — digital for short runs, offset for high volume.

4

Mail prep or delivery

Jobs can move directly into addressing, presort, and postal prep, or be prepared for pickup and delivery.

Frequently asked questions

What file formats do you accept for printing?

We accept PDF, Adobe InDesign packaged files, and Adobe Illustrator files. PDFs should be press-ready with fonts embedded, images at 300 DPI minimum, and bleed included where needed.

How long does printing take?

Turnaround depends on quantity and format. Digital runs under 1,000 pieces typically print within 2–3 business days after proof approval. Offset jobs take 5–7 business days for runs over 5,000. Rush service is available for time-sensitive campaigns.

Can you handle the mailing after printing?

Yes. We print and mail in the same facility. Once your job comes off press, we can move it directly into data processing, addressing, and postal prep without leaving the building.

Do you offer design services?

We provide file review and minor layout adjustments, but full graphic design is handled by our design team. If you need a mail piece designed, ask us about bundling design with your print job.

What is the minimum order quantity?

There is no strict minimum. We've printed jobs as small as 100 postcards for local campaigns and as large as 50,000+ pieces for regional nonprofit appeals. Pricing adjusts based on quantity and complexity.

How do I get pricing?

Call us at (845) 255-5722 or fill out our estimate form with your piece size, quantity, paper preference, and whether you need mailing services. We'll send a quote within one business day.
